compatibility_regressions: The contract requires preserved arbitrary sys.path[0] entries to survive leading/trailing-colon PYTHONPATH cleanup, while the gold patch retains positional cleanup that can remove the preserved entry in those combinations.
The empty-sys.path acceptance check is incompatible with the gold implementation, which raises when evaluating sys.path[0].
invented_requirements: Treating an empty sys.path as a no-op was not requested by the public issue and is not supported by the hindsight gold patch, which still indexes sys.path[0].
Requiring PYTHONPATH colon cleanup to identify working-directory entries without relying on the existing positional logic expands the requested fix beyond guarding the initial removal.
Requiring a dedicated runpy regression and broader contractual coverage for empty sys.path and all PYTHONPATH interactions exceeds the supplied issue and hindsight test patch.
material_blockers: The sealed contract mandates behavior that conflicts with the hindsight implementation oracle for empty sys.path and arbitrary-first-entry PYTHONPATH-colon combinations; those additions must be removed or explicitly classified as intentional scope beyond the audited issue.
redundant_questions: The first interview question reconfirmed the exact three-value rule already stated explicitly in the public request.
The final approval question repeated the consolidated contract after the material choices had already been answered.
summary: The interview accurately recalled repository structure and preserved every explicit owner answer, but it converted interviewer-introduced robustness and test ideas into mandatory behavior. Hindsight confirms the core exact-value guard and preservation of an unrelated leading path, while showing that empty-path handling and retargeted PYTHONPATH cleanup were not part of the accepted implementation. The contract therefore is not implementation-ready against the audited issue-time scope.
